solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disregard kid, one not always at work before time

parts.note: to kid someone is to con them
a temp works only intermittently, filling in for others

explanation.surface: Someone shows disdain for a youngster who is only an occasional worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is scorn, a deliberate disregard for someone or something.

clue.text: Muscle fatigue caused by runs in military stations

indicators.note: in places the runs letter inside the stations

parts.note: camps are military bases
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Soldiers' aches come from running around their barracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Cramps are painful muscle contractions, often after tiring exertion.

clue.text: Contracted one engaged in efficient energy deal

indicators.note: engaged in means involved within, so these letters go inside

parts.note: neat means tidy and efficient
to contract flu is to get, got, it
I is the Roman numeral one
E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A signed-up party enters an energy-saving agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' looks like signing up but means caught, as an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To negotiate is to bargain, so it serves as the verb deal.

clue.text: Inexpensive ecstasy active in entertaining

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: in places the active word within the funny one

parts.note: comical means amusing
a machine that is on is active

explanation.surface: A cheap pill is busy being fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Economical means thrifty or cheap to run, so it matches inexpensive.

clue.text: One is sitting in a part of the theatre reserved for musicians?

definitions.text: One is sitting in a part of the theatre reserved for musicians?

indicators.note: sitting in means placed inside the next part

parts.words: a part of the theatre reserved for musicians
parts.note: the orchestra pit is where the musicians play
an is the indefinite article, meaning one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone seated in the orchestra pit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a keyboard player in the orchestra pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard player sits in the orchestra pit during a show.

clue.text: Catch, pulled back, is hard to dislodge

indicators.note: pulled back tells us to read the synonym for catch from right to left

parts.note: to catch a thief is to nab him
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Something caught and hauled in is stuck fast and tough to shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled back' turns NAB into BAN; the definition is a little oblique.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish is to drive away or expel, so it can stand for dislodge.

clue.text: Guy decapitated a family member

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: to guy is to mock or taunt

explanation.surface: A man beheaded one of his relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is the verb meaning to ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister is a relative, one of the family.

clue.text: Publication is to instigate litigation

parts.note: to sue is to bring a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A magazine goes to court.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is one edition of a magazine or newspaper.

clue.text: People detained by army a relatively long time

parts.note: a host is an archaic word for an army
ages means a long while

explanation.surface: Prisoners held by soldiers for a good while.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostages are captives held as security, people detained.

clue.text: Climbing a track

parts.note: a scent is a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: Going up a path.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is the act of climbing, the noun sense of climbing.

clue.text: A mixture of grog responsible for offensive behaviour

indicators.note: a mixture is a stirring-together, so the letters of grog are jumbled

explanation.surface: Drinking a blend of rum and water leads to bad conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture of' signals the rearrangement. The answer is British slang for aggressive trouble-making, and grog is rum and water.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is informal British slang for aggressive, troublesome conduct.

clue.text: Child is adopted by arts people with a burning desire

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so these letters go inside the arts

parts.note: taken as written
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A boy is taken up by the creative world, people with real passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire-raisers literally want things to burn, a humorous reading of a passionate yearning.

clue.text: Condescending person gently hit upstanding individual carrying on

parts.note: a pat is a gentle tap

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the next word sits inside

parts.note: a riser is literally someone who stands up
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gives a light tap to an honest person who keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' looks like praise for a decent person, but it literally describes one who gets to their feet; 'carrying' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A patroniser treats others with condescension, talking down to them.

clue.text: Fix a bristle-like appendage

parts.note: to fix something in place is to set it

explanation.surface: Attach a hairlike growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A seta is a zoological term for a bristle or bristle-shaped structure on an animal.

clue.text: Study work reflected in reference

indicators.note: in places the reflected word inside the reference

parts.note: a citation is a reference to a source

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the word for work is read backwards

parts.note: a machine that goes works

explanation.surface: Research shown in a bibliography.
explanation.definitionFit: Cogitation is deep thought, as is study in the sense of a brown study.

clue.text: Roman Catholic is spotted in trading centre

indicators.note: something spotted in a place is located inside it

parts.note: a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A Catholic is seen at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: A Marist is a member of a Roman Catholic religious order devoted to Mary.

clue.text: Tenderfoot returned covered in the radioactive mineral

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by the following word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: returned asks for the novice word to be read backwards

parts.note: a tiro is a beginner or novice

explanation.surface: A novice came back coated with the radioactive stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives ORIT, and 'covered in' wraps it. A tenderfoot is a beginner, originally American slang for a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorite is a thorium silicate ore, a radioactive mineral.

clue.text: One air vent buckled maintaining pressure behind closed doors

indicators.note: maintaining means holding within, so the pressure letter is inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: buckled means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A warped vent keeps its pressure secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buckled' rearranges I and AIRVENT into INRIVATE; 'maintaining' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Done behind closed doors means done privately, out of public view.

clue.text: Isolated contaminated crops containing commercial form of iodine

indicators.note: containing means holding inside
contaminated means corrupted, so the letters of crops are jumbled

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Isolated spoiled crops hold a commercial iodine product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contaminated' gives SPORC from the crops, and 'containing' wraps the advert and iodine symbol inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means scattered or isolated, happening only here and there.

clue.text: Quiet one handling whistle-blower's introduction

indicators.note: handling means holding, so the official sits within the other letters

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
an ace is a one in cards
a referee blows the whistle; ref is short for referee

explanation.surface: A discreet person deals with an informant's opening remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whistle-blower looks like an informant but is a football referee.
explanation.definitionFit: A preface is the introductory section at the start of a book.

clue.text: Number 12 using only the centre square?

indicators.note: using only the centre means keep the middle letters and drop the ends

parts.note: the figure 12 written as a word
square means level or quits, even

explanation.surface: A figure on a board limited to the middle tile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using only the centre' keeps EL from TWELVE, dropping TW and VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is a number, one less than a dozen.

clue.text: Pinches lawbreakers seizing power

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the power letter goes inside

parts.note: crims is informal for criminals

explanation.surface: Thieves who grab power steal things.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimp is to pinch or press into small folds or ridges.

clue.text: Gets friendly with bowlers, say, taking part in sporting contest

indicators.note: taking part in means being inside the contest

parts.note: a cup is a sporting competition
bowler hats are hats, as the say signals

explanation.surface: Cricket bowlers chat during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The bowlers look like cricketers but are bowler hats.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat someone up is to talk to them flirtatiously, getting friendly.

clue.text: Irritates fishermen paying no attention to line

indicators.note: paying no attention to means ignoring, so the letter is omitted

parts.note: anglers fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Anglers ignore their lines and annoy people.
explanation.definitionFit: Angers means annoys or irritates, the same verb form.

clue.text: Piece offered by jeweller in gold?

definitions.text: Piece offered by jeweller in gold?

indicators.note: the letters are offered by the run of words that follows, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A goldsmith presents a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of 'jeweller' and 'in g'; the whole clue doubles as its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A band worn on the finger is the archetypal piece a jeweller sells in gold.

clue.text: Drifter turned on lunatic

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the little word reads backwards

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A wanderer was attacked by a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad wanders from place to place, a drifter.

clue.text: Split peas spoiled a small amount of food

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined, so the letters of peas are disordered

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance of food

explanation.surface: Divided peas went off, a meagre portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A split is a division or parting, a noun meaning separation.

clue.text: Types occupying prison cells in the past

indicators.note: occupying means filling a space inside the next words

explanation.surface: Characters were once locked in jail cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Types' is padding; the answer straddles prison and cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some earlier time.

clue.text: Bullies primed device with activists about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so activists go round the device

parts.note: doers are people who act
a mine is an explosive device that can be primed

explanation.surface: Thugs prepared a bomb with militants around them.
explanation.definitionFit: To domineer is to bully or lord it over others, so bullies is the same verb form.

clue.text: Cross that is worn by traitor

indicators.note: worn by means enclosed by, so the betrayer goes inside

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a rat is a betrayer

explanation.surface: A turncoat wears a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross as an adjective means angry, which is what irate says.

clue.text: Club's food that's reprocessed and set

parts.note: cud is food chewed again by cattle
to gel is to set like jelly

explanation.surface: A society's meal is recycled and firmed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cudgel is a short heavy stick used as a weapon, a club.

clue.text: They have made mistakes blocking Pakistan's opening bowlers

indicators.note: blocking means getting in the way, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: sinners are people who have done wrong

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Errant players hold up Pakistan's opening attack.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, spinners are bowlers who make the ball turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinners are a kind of cricket bowler who impart spin to the ball.
